changes.finding: C06 submitted pending writes versus deterministically active and queued worker states
changes.before: Abandon settles active and queued writes, broken pipe gives Closed, and drop after a completed last write delivers EOF.
changes.after: The abandon test requires the two submitted pending writes and a later write to return Closed, without synchronizing that either submitted write has become active in the worker. Broken pipe gives Closed, and drop after a completed last write delivers EOF.
changes.reason: in_order polls its first future before its second; nesting it submits both writes before abandon. The test has no worker-progress acknowledgment or barrier before abandon, so both jobs may still be queued. It requires settlement of the two submitted pending writes and Closed for a later write, without establishing deterministic exercise of both current and queue paths. Broken-pipe and completed-last-write EOF descriptions remain unchanged.

implementation_context_distinct_from_tes.statement: Writer::abandon handles an optional current reply and drains queued jobs, but those implementation branches do not establish which worker states this unsynchronized source test reaches.

additional_inputs.used_for: Writer::write queues a job and awaits its reply (75–85); abandon handles current and queue (101–110, 157–166); the separate worker sets current and calls write_all (113–151). These support the implementation-versus-test-coverage distinction and the decision to leave implementation-only dependents unchanged.
